post.caption:
Per terawatt-hour produced, nuclear has one of the lowest death rates of any energy source, including renewables, and that figure includes Chernobyl and Fukushima. The gap comes from how the harm arrives: coal kills continuously and invisibly through air quality, nuclear kills rarely and memorably. The energy density is extreme, so waste volumes are small. The honest drawbacks are cost, build time and long-lived waste. The numbers are surprising on their own.
